title: God Puts Empty Worship on Trial
overview: God calls his people into a kind of courtroom, not to fault their offerings, but to say he wants gratitude, trust and an honest life to go with them.

parts.label: The court is called (vv. 1-6)
parts.note: God appears from Zion, the temple hill in Jerusalem, with fire and storm that recall the giving of the law at Mount Sinai, and calls heaven and earth as witnesses. He summons his own people, who had sealed their covenant (a binding agreement) with him by sacrifice, an old custom of cutting an animal to make a promise official.

parts.label: God has no need of offerings (vv. 7-13)
parts.note: God says he has no complaint about the offerings themselves, since the people bring them constantly. The problem is treating him as if he were hungry or in their debt, when every animal on earth already belongs to him.

parts.label: What God actually wants (vv. 14-15)
parts.note: He asks for thanks offered from the heart, promises kept, and trust that turns to him in trouble. He promises to rescue those who call, and their rescue will bring him honor.

parts.label: Words without a changed life (vv. 16-21)
parts.note: God now turns to those who recite his laws yet go along with theft, adultery, lies and slandering their own family. Because God had not acted yet, they assumed he was as careless about wrong as they were.

parts.label: A final warning and promise (vv. 22-23)
parts.note: God warns those who forget him that he will tear them to pieces with no one to rescue them, a harsh threat the psalm states plainly. It ends by tying real thanks to an honest way of living, and promises God's rescue to those who live that way.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the psalm only criticizes sacrifice offered without a sincere heart, which many scholars see as its plain sense, or also hints that animal sacrifice itself would one day be set aside, as some Christians read it in light of Jesus.
think: When does a ritual or habit in your life feel like it truly means something, and when does it start to feel like going through the motions?
